bootstrap.resampling_design: PAIRED per (source, region, metric_a, metric_b): metric_a and metric_b are computed from the SAME physical windows (same underlying rows), so each bootstrap iteration draws ONE shared window resample and re-derives both metrics' aggregate rankings from it -- unlike the sealed cross-source comparison, which resamples two genuinely independent window populations independently.
bootstrap.seed_rule: deterministic: zlib.crc32('|'.join([source, region, metric_a, metric_b])) -- depends only on the condition/metric-pair identity, not on iteration order, so re-running any subset of conditions reproduces identical seeds.

direction_rule: Every metric value is direction-normalized so HIGHER is always better before any ranking comparison: HIGHER_BETTER metrics pass through unchanged; LOWER_BETTER metrics are negated. compare_rankings() is then always invoked with higher_is_better=True. This is a pure value transform applied independently per metric; it never changes which (window, policy) observations are defined.

bh_fdr.family_definition: All PRIMARY policy-pair disagreement tests that reached the statistical-support stage (both p_a and p_b computed) within ONE (source, region, metric_a, metric_b) condition -- i.e. up to C(11,2)=55 policy pairs per family. Mirrors the sealed reversal contract's family definition ("all pairwise reversal tests within one load level"), generalized from "one condition, fixed metric" to "one metric-pair, fixed condition".
bh_fdr.per_pair_p_value: max(p_a, p_b) -- intersection-union combination of the two metrics' block-bootstrap sign-test p-values, read off the same resamples as the CI rule (no new inferential procedure), mirroring reversal_analysis.py's p_x/p_y convention.

disagreement_classification.threshold_dimensional_justification: The margin is winning_value_minus_losing_value / |losing_value|, computed independently within EACH metric's own units -- a dimensionless, self-relative ratio. Requiring both metric_a's own margin and metric_b's own margin to exceed 10% (an intersection-union test) never compares metric_a's units to metric_b's units directly, so heterogeneous units (seconds vs a fraction vs requests/second) do not invalidate the threshold. Verified before adoption, not mechanically assumed.
disagreement_classification.threshold_reused_from: docs/RANKING_PORTABILITY_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md §A reversal practical-margin rule (REVERSAL_PRACTICAL_MARGIN_FRACTION = 0.10), reused unchanged.

label: POST_PHASE12_RESULT_INDEPENDENT_ANALYSIS_EXTENSION
metric_pair_selection_rule: ALL unordered pairs among eligible metrics; no pair added, removed, or reordered based on any observed correlation, reversal, or disagreement magnitude.
min_common_policies_rationale: At n=2 common policies, Kendall tau-b is degenerate (only +1/-1 possible, no real distribution). n=3 is the smallest common-policy count at which tau-b is non-degenerate. Frozen before any real Phase-12 row was read by this extension's code.
policy_panel_note: PRIMARY_ONLY (11); STYLE_APPROXIMATION policies excluded from headline cross-metric results, per docs/RANKING_PORTABILITY_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md's robustness stratum rule.
undefined_rule: Never zero-imputed. A policy with an undefined (NaN/None) value for a metric in a given condition is excluded from that metric's aggregate only (docs/RANKING_PORTABILITY_METRIC_DEFINITIONS.md, reused unchanged). If the resulting common-defined-policy count is below min_common_policies, the record's status is UNDEFINED_INSUFFICIENT_COMMON_POLICIES and all statistics are null -- the record is still emitted, never omitted.
